examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For each input, map every present state to an output and next state. Minimize a Mealy machine by initially grouping identical output vectors, then splitting groups whenever their next states enter different groups. Repeat to a fixed point. For a Moore machine the initial groups are based on state outputs instead.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
States A,B have output vectors (0,1) and transitions A:(C,D), B:(C,D). C,D are in different stable classes. How many states are required for the pair {A,B} after minimization?

**Answer: 1.** A and B have identical outputs for both inputs and identical successor states. No future input can distinguish them, regardless of C,D being different. The pair merges to one state.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Reachability and equivalence are separate checks. Remove unreachable states when minimizing a machine specified with an initial state.

The minimum number of state bits does not guarantee the simplest combinational implementation.
